key_insight: For probabilistic SST forecasting, learned advection–diffusion physics offered no reliable benefit, while lead-wise variance calibration consistently improved uncertainty estimates.
engineering_relevance: Prioritize calibration and verify that current data add predictive information before investing in explicit transport architectures.
method: Compared physics-loss and explicit-transport variants of a heteroscedastic ConvLSTM.
Tested learned versus supplied currents using input channels, transport steps and frozen-current numerical forecasts.
Evaluated lead-wise variance scaling and fine-tuning on 15-day rollouts.
evidence_signal: Tests used Bay of Bengal NOAA OISST v2.1 data (1982–2024) and controlled synthetic currents; the real-data physics loss changed day-15 CRPS by −0.007°C (95% interval: −0.022 to +0.008), while calibration reduced day-1 CRPS by 13–21%.
watch_item: Learned currents were not identifiable in these tests, and reanalysis-driven transport worsened short-lead forecasts; the paper also withdraws an earlier uncontrolled claim of an 81% CRPS reduction.
paper_title: Where Should Physics Enter? Information, Identifiability and Calibration in Probabilistic Sea Surface Temperature Forecasting
